title: Support --help after a command
lead: `obfuscator <command> --help` (or `-h`) prints the usage text and exits 0 instead of failing with an unknown-option error.
findings_note: Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs Run: help is recognised only as the first argument; 'obfuscate --help' now fails with Unknown option '--help' (before ob-07 it failed with a missing-option error)
boundary: **Not in this slice:** per-command help text (the full usage is printed); bare `help` after a command; help for an unknown command (still fails with "Unknown command."); library (`Obfuscator/`) changes.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Help is recognised only as the first argument (`Run` checks `IsHelp(args[0])`). Since ob-07, `obfuscator obfuscate --help` fails with `Unknown option '--help' for 'obfuscate'.` and exit 1, although asking a command for help is the most common way users discover its options.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Obfuscator.Cli/ObfuscatorCliProgram.cs; Obfuscator.Tests/ObfuscatorTests.cs; Obfuscator.Cli/README.md, Obfuscator.Cli/PackageReadme.md and README.md where they describe help.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `generate --help`, `obfuscate --help`, `deobfuscate -h` print the usage text to stdout and exit 0.
- Help anywhere after a known command wins, including in a value slot: `obfuscate --input missing.csv --help` and `obfuscate --output --help` exit 0, print usage, and read or write no files.
- Help wins over other argument errors on the same line (unknown option, inline `--passphrase=...`) without echoing any value.
- Case follows option matching: `--HELP` after a command is help.
- Bare `help` after a command is not help (still rejected as before).
- An unknown command with `--help` still fails with "Unknown command." and exit 1.
- Existing top-level `--help`, `-h`, `help` and no-argument behaviour is unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: In `Run`, after the command name matches a known command and before its options are parsed, return `PrintUsage()` with exit 0 when any later argument is `--help` (case-insensitive, like options) or `-h`. Leave `IsHelp` and the top-level check as they are. Mention `obfuscator <command> --help` in the usage text and in the docs that show `obfuscator --help`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Run the focused CLI tests, then `dotnet test Obfuscator.slnx` and `scripts/test-local.sh`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Only CLI argument handling, its tests and docs change.
